This group comprises coal, a combustible black (hard coal) and brownish-black (brown coal) rock consisting of more than 50% by weight and more than 70% by volume of carbonaceous material. It is formed from plant remains that have been compacted, hardened and chemically altered, and metamorphosed by heat and pressure over geologic time.

This class comprises black coal ranked as hard coal, which includes anthracite and bituminous coal. Hard coal refers to coal of gross calorific value equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis and with a mean random reflectance of vitrinite of at least 0.6%.

This subclass comprises anthracite, a high rank hard, lustrous black coal destined primarily for residential and industrial (as steel making) or commercial applications. It has generally less than 10% volatile matter and a high carbon content (about 90% fixed carbon). Its gross calorific value is equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis.

High rank hard lustrous black coal destined primarily for residential and industrial (as steel making) or commercial applications. It has generally less than 10% volatile matter and a high carbon content (about 90% fixed carbon). Its gross calorific value is equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis.

This subclass comprises coking or metallurgical coal and other bituminous coal. Bituminous coal is a medium rank coal used for gasification, industrial coking and heat raising, and residential heat raising. It is characterized by higher volatile matter than anthracite (more than 10%) and lower carbon content (less than 90% fixed carbon). Its gross calorific value is equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis.

Bituminous coal with a quality that allows the production of a coke suitable to support a blast furnace charge. Its gross calorific value is equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis.

Other bituminous coal mainly used for steam raising purposes. It is characterized by higher volatile matter than anthracite (more than 10%) and lower carbon content (less than 90% fixed carbon). Its gross calorific value is equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis.

This class comprises softer brown coal, which includes sub-bituminous coal and lignite. Brown coal refers to coal of gross calorific value of less than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis, and a mean random reflectance of vitrinite of less than 0.6%.

This subclass comprises sub-bituminous coal, a non-agglomerating coal with a gross calorific value equal to or greater than 20,000 kJ/kg and less than 24,000 kJ/kg, containing more than 31% volatile matter on a dry mineral matter free basis.

A plant of the genus Cannabis refers generally to three varieties which are cannabis Sativa, cannabis Indica and cannabis Ruderalis. Sativas and Indicas are the most commonly used cannabis strains for cultivation and propagation. The genetics of the different cannabis strains are widely mixed or cloned to create cannabis hybrids. Cannabis contains a number of active elements, including cannabinoids such as tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) or dronabinol, cannabidiol (CBD) and terpenes (aromatic compounds or chemical markers). This group comprises prefabricated buildings that are built in a factory or manufacturing facility and delivered to the construction site, and the components of prefabricated buildings built in a factory to be assembled later at a construction site. Prefabricated (factory-built) buildings are virtually complete and either unassembled or fully assembled (or manufactured) and ready to use; they can also be incomplete buildings, whether or not assembled, having the essential character of factory-built or prefabricated buildings. Prefabricated buildings can be used for residential or non-residential purposes.

A building refers to any roofed independent free-standing permanent construction or structure usually enclosed within external walls or dividing walls that extend from the foundations to the roof and comprises one or more rooms or other space. A building can be entered or accessed by persons or animals and is suitable or intended for protecting them and objects. A building can also include a separately usable underground construction.

A residential building refers to a construction in which at least half of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for residential or dwelling purposes.

A non-residential building refers to a construction in which more than half of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for non-residential purposes.

Code title: Courier, parcel, and local messenger and delivery services
Code definition: This class comprises station-to-station transportation of small packages and documents without tracking; courier and messenger services; and neighbourhood delivery of small purchased items.

Code title: Station-to-station transportation of small packages and documents without tracking
Code definition: This subclass comprises transportation of small packages and documents without tracking of each package and document. Service is typically station-to-station but may be door-to-door. Transportation is provided on passenger buses and trains according to published schedules but departure and arrival times are not guaranteed. May include collect on delivery (C.O.D.) service. May include declared value coverage.

Code title: Station-to-station transportation of small packages and documents without tracking
Code definition: Transportation of small packages and documents without tracking of each package and document. Service is typically station-to-station but may be door-to-door. Transportation is provided on passenger buses and trains according to published schedules but departure and arrival times are not guaranteed. May include collect on delivery (C.O.D.) service. May include declared value coverage.

This subclass comprises transportation and delivery, by a definite day and possibly by a definite time, of small packages and documents, with tracking of each package and document. Delivery by the scheduled day or specified time may be guaranteed. Small packages usually can be handled by one person without using special equipment. Service is typically door-to-door, although there may be options for the shipper to drop a package off and for the receiver to pick it up, and occasional shippers may have to drop off their packages. Pick-up and delivery outside normal service area or outside normal service hours, and pick-up on demand or on a regular schedule, are covered here. Service may include customs clearance. May include collect on delivery (C.O.D.) service. May include declared value coverage.

Transportation and delivery, on the same day as pick-up and possibly by a definite time, of small packages and documents, with tracking of each package and document. Delivery on the day or by the specified time may be guaranteed. Small packages usually can be handled by one person without using special equipment. Service is typically door-to-door, although there may be options for the shipper to drop a package off and for the receiver to pick it up, and occasional shippers may have to drop off their packages. Pick-up and delivery outside normal service area or outside normal service hours, and pick-up on demand or on a regular schedule, are covered here. Service may include customs clearance. May include collect on delivery (C.O.D.) service. May include declared value coverage.

Transportation and delivery, on the first business day or first calendar day following pick-up, and possibly by a definite time, of small packages and documents, with tracking of each package and document. Delivery by the scheduled day or specified time may be guaranteed. Small packages usually can be handled by one person without using special equipment. Service is typically door-to-door, although there may be options for the shipper to drop a package off and for the receiver to pick it up, and occasional shippers may have to drop off their packages. Pick-up and delivery outside normal service area or outside normal service hours, and pick-up on demand or on a regular schedule, are covered here. Service may include customs clearance. May include collect on delivery (C.O.D.) service. May include declared value coverage.

Code title: Second-day or later courier and messenger services
Code definition: Transportation and delivery, on the second business day or second calendar day following pick-up, or on a later specified day, and possibly by a definite time, of small packages and documents, with tracking of each package and document. Delivery by the scheduled day or specified time may be guaranteed. Small packages usually can be handled by one person without using special equipment. Service is typically door-to-door, although there may be options for the shipper to drop a package off and for the receiver to pick it up, and occasional shippers may have to drop off their packages. Pick-up and delivery outside normal service area or outside normal service hours, and pick-up on demand or on a regular schedule, are covered here. Service may include customs clearance. May include collect on delivery (C.O.D.) service. May include declared value coverage.

Code title: Neighbourhood delivery of small purchased items
Code definition: This subclass comprises door-to-door transportation and delivery of small purchased and serviced items such as take-out meals, groceries, prescription drugs and dry-cleaned clothes. Service is limited to a specified neighbourhood. Delivery is made immediately after the item is purchased or ordered, or scheduled within a short time. Expected delivery time is made known to the recipient. May include collect on delivery (C.O.D.) service.

This group comprises urban transit services; taxi and limousine services; interurban and rural bus passenger transportation services; school bus services; other transit and passenger transportation services by road; rail passenger transportation services; water passenger transportation services; air passenger transportation services; and scenic and sightseeing tour services. Rental and leasing services of passenger vehicles with operator, driver or crew are included.

This class comprises passenger transportation operated on a network of regular routes and on regular schedules. Service is centred on an urban area and covers urban and suburban areas and areas from which they draw commuters. Commuter services that primarily carry passengers to and from the urban centre are included. Transportation may involve one or more types of vehicles, such as buses, subways, streetcars, commuter trains and ferries. Passengers are permitted to pay on a per-trip basis, and the fare may be calculated on a zone basis. Covers urban transit services whether paid for by passengers or by contracts.

This class comprises local limousine services; local taxi services and taxi dispatch services.

This subclass comprises local passenger transportation by luxury automobile, not operated on regular schedules or routes, and available only by reservation, or without reservation to passengers as they leave an airport or other transportation terminal. In the case of travel from an airport or other transportation terminal, the fee is on the basis of the distance to the destination, calculated on a zone basis; there may be a minimum charge. In other cases, the fee charged is on the basis of the length of time for which the vehicle is reserved; there is normally a minimum length of time and/or a minimum tariff. The vehicle and driver are available to make a series of trips as directed by the customer during the period for which the vehicle has been reserved.

Code title: Local taxi services and taxi dispatch services
Code definition: This subclass comprises passenger transportation by automobile, not operated on regular schedules or routes, and available on demand. The fee charged to passengers is on the basis of distance travelled. Also comprises taxi dispatch services.

Code title: Interurban and rural bus passenger transportation services
Code definition: This class comprises long distance passenger transportation by road, over fixed routes on a regular schedule. Long distance transportation is generally between metropolitan areas. Service is either part of an interurban network and connecting services to other destinations are available or service is intended to serve a particular destination, and is not designed to connect to a network of interurban service. Covers charges for incidental transportation of passenger baggage.

This class comprises transportation of students between home and school on a regular basis. Service is operated on regular routes and schedules that are designed to accommodate the home locations of individual passengers. The vehicles used are typically buses but may include smaller vehicles such as vans and cars, and may include vehicles accessible to people using wheelchairs and other mobility aids. Passengers are not charged a per-trip fee. Covers school bus services whether paid for by passengers or by contracts.

Code definition: This class comprises long distance passenger transportation by chartered bus; local passenger transportation by chartered bus; other long distance passenger transportation services by road (except fixed route); shuttle service; other local fixed route passenger transportation service by road; special needs urban transit service; and local shared-ride passenger transportation service. Rental or leasing services of road passenger transportation vehicles with operator or driver are included.

Code title: Long distance passenger transportation by chartered bus
Code definition: This subclass comprises long distance passenger transportation for a specific occasion by road vehicles with sufficient interior height for a person to stand, typically buses but not limousines or taxis, with driver. Service is not operated on regular schedules or routes, and is available only by reservation of the entire vehicle, for which a fee is charged to the party who makes the reservation. The party who makes the reservation may or may not charge the passengers an explicit fee for the transportation. Covers use of vehicles that are accessible to passengers using wheelchairs and other mobility aids.

Code definition: This subclass comprises long distance passenger transportation by luxury automobile, not operated on regular schedules or routes, and available only by reservation. The operator carries as many parties having similar origins or destinations as can be accommodated on each trip.

Code definition: Long distance passenger transportation by luxury automobile, not operated on regular schedules or routes, and available only by reservation. The operator carries as many parties having similar origins or destinations as can be accommodated on each trip.

This subclass comprises passenger transportation operated on regular routes and on regular schedules or on regular routes on an unscheduled but frequent basis. Service is typically between a limited number of pick-up and drop-off points, with no local service for other points along the route; or on a circular route with frequent stops. The service is not part of a network. As many passengers as can be accommodated are carried on a first-come first-served basis. Passengers may or may not be charged a per-trip fee. Covers shuttle service whether paid for by passengers or by contracts.

Code title: Other local fixed route passenger transportation services by road
Code definition: This subclass comprises local fixed route passenger transportation service by road except urban transit service, transportation of students between home and school on a regular basis, and shuttle service. Covers employee transportation to work arranged by the employer and operated on regular routes and schedules. Vehicles used are typically buses but may be smaller vehicles such as vans and cars, and may be accessible to people using wheelchairs and other mobility aids. Passengers are not charged a per-trip fee. Covers employee transportation to work whether paid for by passengers or by contracts. Carpool transportation is provided by arranging and administering pools and providing a vehicle to members of each pool in exchange for a monthly fee to cover operating costs. One or more pool members must act as driver.

Passengers are transported to and from their individual homes, workplaces and other locations. Passengers are charged a per-trip fee. Covers special needs urban transit service whether paid for by passengers or by contracts.

Code title: Rental of road passenger transportation vehicles, with operator
Code definition: This subclass comprises rental or operating leasing services of passenger automobiles and light vans with operator or driver, that is, chauffeur-driven car-hire services, wherever delivered, generally supplied on a time basis to a limited number of passengers and frequently involving transportation to more than one destination. Also comprises rental or operating leasing services of buses or coaches with operator or driver for a period of time, not generally dependent on distance. The renter defines how and when the vehicles will be operated, determining schedules, routes, and other operational considerations.

This class comprises interurban transportation of passengers by rail.
This subclass comprises interurban transportation of passengers by rail.

Code title: Passenger rail transportation services, business class
Code definition: Interurban transportation of passengers by rail, with premium-quality amenities, without sleeping facilities. The fare is not subject to advance purchase requirements or restrictions on exchanges or refunds. Covers the transport of accompanying luggage and other items as well as sales to passengers and bulk purchases by tour operators of seats for resale; exclusive and non-exclusive car usage; and scheduled and non-scheduled services. May include a segment where transportation is by bus. Covers service paid for with a ticket or voucher from a book of tickets, or with a train pass.

Code title: Passenger rail transportation services, economy/discounted economy classes
Code definition: Interurban transportation of passengers by rail, with standard-quality amenities, without sleeping facilities. Food and beverages are available at an extra charge. This class comprises coastal and Great Lakes fixed route passenger transportation services by water; and other passenger transportation services by water. Rental and leasing services of water passenger transportation vessels with operator or crew are included.

Code title: Other passenger transportation services by water
Code definition: Transportation of passengers by water on fixed routes within harbours, transportation of passengers by water on fixed routes on inland waters except the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Seaway, and transportation of passengers by water, not on fixed routes. This class comprises scheduled and chartered air passenger transportation services. Rental and leasing of passenger aircraft with operator or crew (wet and damp leasing) are included.

Code title: Scheduled air passenger transportation services (except wet and damp leasing)

This subclass comprises rental and leasing of complete aircraft and crew, for the chartered or non-scheduled transportation of passengers and their accompanying baggage, equipment and supplies. Renters or lessees generally do not have operational control of the flights. Air charter services include air taxi, ad hoc air charter, frequent charter membership and full charter services. Full (public) air charter is a long-term renting of an entire aircraft, usually undertaken by tour operators, that require aircraft on a seasonal basis, but do not have the required infrastructure to operate their own aircraft.

Code title: Air passenger charter transportation services, domestic
Code definition: Rental and leasing of complete aircraft and crew, for the non-scheduled transportation of passengers and their accompanying baggage, equipment and supplies, within Canada. Covers positioning fees, layover fees, and pilot standby fees. Renters or lessees generally do not have operational control of the flights.

Covers positioning fees, layover fees, and pilot standby fees. Renters or lessees generally do not have operational control of the flights.

Code title: Rental and leasing of passenger aircraft with operator or crew (except chartering)
Code definition: This subclass comprises rental and leasing services of passenger aircraft or aircraft suitable for passenger and freight (including helicopters) with operator or crew (wet and damp leasing). A ''wet lease'' is a leasing arrangement whereby one "airline" or aircraft operator (the lessor) provides an aircraft, complete crew (''damp lease'' is with only cockpit crew), maintenance, and insurance (ACMI). These services are generally supplied on a time basis and several different destinations are frequently involved. The services may include providing fuel. Renters or lessees generally have operational control of the flights. The period of the rental or lease can go from one month to usually one to two years. Everything less than one month can be considered as ad-hoc charter services.

This group comprises residential buildings.

A residential building refers to a construction in which at least half of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for residential or private dwelling purposes, whether on a permanent basis or not. Residential buildings normally provide accommodation units or residential building units with self-contained and exclusive use of bathroom and kitchen facilities to the occupants of each unit. At least half of the useful floor area must be used or intended for dwelling units, in the case of apartment buildings. A residential building unit is a structurally separated and independent place.
A group of three row houses that are attached is considered to be three separate buildings if their external walls or dividing walls extend from the foundations to the roof.

Residential buildings constructed entirely at the building site, as well as on-site fully assembled precast, panelized, modular and other prefabricated residential buildings are included in this group. Unassembled prefabricated residential buildings built in a factory, and manufactured or fully assembled residential buildings built in a factory and delivered ready for move-in, are excluded from this group.

A building for which the majority of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for dwelling units with shared bathroom and kitchen, or that area is used primarily to offer care and other assisted living services, is classified as a "collective dwelling-type building" under the non-residential buildings group.

A building refers to any independent free-standing permanent structure comprising one or more residential dwelling units, business units or other spaces. A building can be entered by persons or animals and is suitable or intended for protecting them and objects. A building is covered by a roof and is usually enclosed within external walls or dividing walls that extend from the foundations to the roof. In the case of interconnected structures (e.g., semi-detached or terraced houses), any unit separated from other units by a fire wall extending from roof to cellar is considered an individual building. If there is no fire wall, the interconnected building units are regarded as individual buildings if they have their own access (own entrance) as well as their own utility system and are separately usable.

This group comprises research and experimental development services in natural sciences, engineering and technology, medical and health sciences, agricultural and veterinary sciences, social sciences, and humanities and the arts. Research and experimental development (R&D) comprise creative and systemic work undertaken in order to increase the stock of knowledge - including knowledge of humankind, culture and society - and to devise new applications of available knowledge. The term R&D refers to three types of activity: basic research, applied research and experimental development. Basic research refers to experimental or theoretical work undertaken primarily to acquire new knowledge of the underlying foundations of phenomena and observable facts, without any particular application or use in view. Applied research refers to original investigation undertaken in order to acquire new knowledge. It is, however, directed primarily towards a specific, practical aim or objective. Experimental development is systematic work, drawing on knowledge gained from research and practical experience and producing additional knowledge, which is directed to producing new products or processes or to improving existing products or processes.

Research services consist of systematic investigation carried by means of experiment or analysis to achieve a scientific or technological advance such as acquiring new knowledge of the underlying foundation of phenomena and observable facts. Experimental development services consist of new or substantially improved goods, services, systems, methods or processes.

Code title: Licensing of rights for commercial use of sound recordings
Code definition: This subclass comprises licences for the use of sound recordings to generate revenues.

Code title: Licensing of rights for commercial use of sound recordings
Code definition: Licences for the use of sound recordings to generate revenues.

Code title: Licensing of rights for commercial use of dramatic works, and other copyrighted property n.e.c.
Code definition: This class comprises licences for the use of dramatic works, and other copyrighted property n.e.c. to generate revenues.

Code definition: This subclass comprises licences for the use of audiovisual works to generate revenues.

Code definition: Licences for the use of audiovisual works to generate revenues.

Code definition: This subclass comprises licences for the use of dramatic works, except audiovisual works, and of copyrighted property n.e.c. to generate revenues.

Code title: Licensing of rights for commercial use of other dramatic works, and copyrighted property n.e.c.
Code definition: Licences for the use of dramatic works, except audiovisual works, and of copyrighted property n.e.c. to generate revenues.
This class comprises the right to broadcast a sporting event on traditional electronic media and other media rights related to sporting events.
This subclass comprises the right to broadcast a sporting event on traditional electronic media and other media rights related to sporting events.
Rights to broadcast a sporting event on radio or television.
Media rights for sporting events, except broadcasting rights for radio and television.

Code title: Fees for the distribution of television and radio program channels (affiliation payments)
Code definition: This class comprises the right (affiliation payments) for the distribution of a television or audio channel to end users.

Code title: Fees for the distribution of television and radio program channels (affiliation payments)
Code definition: This subclass comprises the right (affiliation payments) for the distribution of a television or audio channel to end users.

Code title: Affiliation payments for the distribution of television channels
Code definition: Rights (affiliation payments) for the distribution of a television channel to end users.

Code title: Affiliation payments for the distribution of audio channels
Code definition: Rights (affiliation payments) for the distribution of an audio channel to end users.

Code title: Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services
Code definition: This group comprises fixed wholesale and retail telecommunications services; fixed wholesale and retail Internet access services; mobile wholesale and retail telecommunications services; cable, satellite, Internet and other fixed or mobile broadcasting distribution services of audiovisual and audio works; and online games, except gambling.
This class comprises fixed wholesale telecommunications and Internet access services, and mobile wholesale telecommunications.

Code title: Fixed wholesale telecommunications services (except Internet access)
Code definition: This subclass comprises the provision of a fixed telecommunications service or facility by a telecommunications service provider to a provider of retail fixed telecommunications services. The purchaser may resell the service or facility to another entity, or use the service or facility to support the services it bills.

Code title: Fixed wholesale telecommunications services (except Internet access)
Code definition: Provision of a fixed telecommunications service or facility by a telecommunications service provider to a provider of retail fixed telecommunications services. The purchaser may resell the service or facility to another entity, or use the service or facility to support the services it bills.
This subclass comprises the provision of fixed Internet access and transport services by a telecommunications service provider to a provider of fixed retail Internet access services.
Provision of fixed Internet access and transport services by a telecommunications service provider to a provider of fixed retail Internet access services.

This subclass comprises the provision of a mobile telecommunications service or facility by a wireless telecommunications service provider to another to exchange traffic and extend service coverage area.
Provision of a mobile telecommunications service or facility by a wireless telecommunications service provider to another to exchange traffic and extend service coverage area.
This class comprises fixed retail telecommunications and Internet access services, and mobile retail telecommunications.

Code title: Fixed retail telecommunications services (except Internet access)
Code definition: This subclass comprises telephone services to end users where calls originate from a device connected to a landline.

Code title: Fixed local and access telecommunications services (except Internet access), at retail
Code definition: A landline-based telephone service that allows end users to make calls within a defined local area and provides access to a long distance network of the customer's choice.

Code title: Fixed long distance telecommunications services (except Internet access), at retail
Code definition: A landline-based telephone service allowing end users to make calls outside a local calling area.
Telecommunications services making use of data protocols to transmit data over a public network.
Telecommunications network segments for the exclusive use of the client on which no control or signalling is performed by the telecommunications service provider.
This subclass comprises the provision of fixed connections (including fixed wireline and wireless) to the Internet to end users.

Provision of fixed connections to the Internet to end users at download speeds not exceeding 64 Kbps. Dial-up Internet access is one of the oldest forms of Internet access technology. It is also referred to as low or narrowband speed Internet access. Narrowband is generally regarded as a category including any connection with a transmission or download speed of up to 1.5 Mbps.

Code title: Fixed high-speed Internet access services, residential
Code definition: Provision of fixed connections to the Internet to residential end users at download speeds generally greater than 256 Kbps. High-speed Internet is also referred to as broadband Internet, with fixed line types such as cable, digital subscriber line (DSL), terrestrial wireless access, direct-to-home satellite access, and fibre optic services. Even though the lowest speed limit for high-speed Internet is set to 256 Kbps in several countries, broadband is generally regarded as a category including any connection with a transmission or download speed of 1.5 Mbps or greater. Connection with download speed from 256 Kbps up to 1.5 Mbps is sometimes referred to as "wideband" or "lite broadband".

Code title: Fixed high-speed Internet access services, non-residential
Code definition: Provision of fixed connections to the Internet to non-residential or business end users at download speeds greater than 256 Kbps. High-speed Internet is also referred to as broadband Internet, with fixed line types such as cable, digital subscriber line (DSL), terrestrial wireless access, direct-to-home satellite access, and fibre optic services. Even though the lowest speed limit for high-speed Internet is set to 256 Kbps in several countries, broadband is generally regarded as a category including any connection with a transmission or download speed of 1.5 Mbps or greater. Connection with download speed from 256 Kbps up to 1.5 Mbps is sometimes referred to as "wideband" or "lite broadband".
This subclass comprises telecommunication services to end users where voice or data communications originate from, or terminate into, a mobile device connected to a wireless network.

Code title: Mobile local and access telecommunications services, at retail
Code definition: A wireless-based telecommunications service that allows end users to make and receive calls within a defined local area and provides access to a long distance network of the customer's choice. Mobile cell phone plans typically bundle voice and text messaging.

Code title: Mobile long distance telecommunications services, at retail
Code definition: Wireless based telecommunications service allowing end users to make calls outside a local calling area.

A service plan providing end users mobile access to text and multimedia messaging, along with access to the Internet through the cellular network. This service is also referred as "wireless mobile Internet access", at retail.
A service that allows a cell phone subscriber to use his or her mobile device while in the service area of another service provider.

Code title: Broadcasting and online games distribution services
Code definition: This class comprises broadcast distribution services of audiovisual and audio works such as television programs, films, videos, sound recordings, via cable, satellite, Internet and other fixed and mobile distribution streams. Also covers distribution services for online games, except gambling, and installation services for connections to broadcasting distribution networks.
This subclass comprises basic television programming packages distribution services, via fixed or mobile devices.

Code title: Basic television programming packages (except online streaming)
Code definition: Providing a basic package of movie and television programming services, basically to a fixed device, except using online streaming, for a monthly subscription fee. Basic packages are any first level programming package that must be purchased before being able to purchase additional programming packages. The basic programming packages are delivered using traditional over-the-air (OTA), cable and satellite television.

Code title: Online streaming of basic programming packages
Code definition: Providing a basic package of movie and television programming services over the Internet, to a fixed or mobile device, using online streaming, for a monthly subscription fee. Basic packages are any first level programming package that must be purchased before being able to purchase additional programming packages.
This subclass comprises discretionary television programming packages distribution services, via fixed or mobile devices.

Providing movie and television programming services, in addition to those included in a basic package, for an additional monthly subscription fee, generally to a fixed device, except using online streaming. This programming service comprises bundles of channels or à la carte channels. The discretionary television programming packages are delivered using traditional cable and satellite television.

Code title: Online streaming of discretionary programming packages
Code definition: Providing movie and television programming services over the Internet, in addition to those included in a basic package, for an additional monthly subscription fee, to a fixed or mobile device, using online streaming. This programming service comprises bundles of channels or à la carte channels.
This subclass comprises pay-per-view services, via fixed or mobile devices. The broadcaster shows a pay-per-view program at the same broadcast time to everyone ordering it.

Providing services which enable subscribers to television programming packages, to watch a specific program (movie or event) at the same broadcast time, generally at a fixed device, for an additional fee, except using online streaming. The pay-per-view services are delivered using traditional cable and satellite television.

Providing services over the Internet which enable subscribers to television programming packages, to watch a specific program (movie or event) at the same broadcast time, on a fixed or mobile device, using online streaming, for an additional fee.

Code title: Television, movie and video on demand services
Code definition: This subclass comprises pay television, movie and other video on demand services (except pay-per-view), via fixed or mobile devices. Subscribers or viewers of video on demand are allowed to choose and watch broadcasts at any time, for a one time fee paid for each individual video that is on demand (transactional video on demand), or for a monthly or annual subscription fee (subscription video on demand) to have unlimited access to television programs, movies and any other types of videos during the time covered by the subscription.

Code title: Television, movie and video on demand (except online streaming)
Code definition: Providing pay television, movie and other video on demand services (except per-pay-view), generally via fixed devices, except using online streaming. Subscribers or viewers to/of video on demand are allowed to choose and watch broadcasts at any time, usually for a one time fee paid for each individual video that is on demand (transactional video on demand). Video on demand services are delivered using traditional cable and satellite television.

Code title: Online on demand streaming of television, movie and video
Code definition: Providing pay television, movie and other video on demand services (except pay-per-view) over the Internet, via fixed or mobile devices, using online streaming. Subscribers or viewers to/of video on demand are allowed to choose and watch broadcasts at any time, usually for a monthly or annual subscription fee (subscription video on demand) to have unlimited access to television programs, movies and any other types of videos during the time covered by the subscription.

Code title: Satellite radio and online audio streaming services
Code definition: This subclass comprises pay satellite radio and online audio (such as music) streaming services.
Pay satellite radio services.

Providing programming services (including self-programming), over the Internet, that comprise a single payment (fee) or a subscription, to a selection of radio shows, music and other audio recordings, streamed to fixed and mobile devices (Internet audio services). Subscribers are allowed to choose and stream contents at any time during the time covered by the payment or subscription.

This subclass comprises provision of various games to be played online, on a subscription or single payment (fee) basis, except gambling. The games are streamed over the Internet to fixed and mobile devices.
Providing various games to be played online, on a subscription or single payment (fee) basis, except gambling. The games are streamed over the Internet to fixed and mobile devices.

Code title: Installation services for connections to broadcasting distribution networks
Code definition: This subclass comprises services of installing cables on the customer premises and/or installing outlets to connect to the program or broadcasting distribution networks.

Code title: Installation services for connections to broadcasting distribution networks
Code definition: Providing installation of cables on the customer premises and/or installing outlets to connect to the program or broadcasting distribution networks.

Code title: Other information technology (IT) and information services
Code definition: This group comprises data processing, hosting and related services, and other information technology (IT) and information services.

Code title: Data processing, hosting, and related services
Code definition: This class comprises services such as website hosting, application provisioning, business process management, infrastructure provisioning, network management, and information and document transformation.

Code title: Website hosting and domain name registration services
Code definition: This subclass comprises the services of providing the infrastructure to host a customer's website and related files in a location that provides connection to the Internet or make their website accessible via the World Wide Web, and domain name registration services.
Services of providing the infrastructure to host a customer's website and related files in a location that provides connection to the Internet or make their website accessible via the World Wide Web.
Services of providing the registration of a domain name for a customer, by certified registrars and authorized resellers or affiliates.

This subclass comprises the provision of leased software applications from a centralized, hosted, and managed computing environment (including cloud), customized to the needs of individual clients or for multi tenant access.

Code title: Application service provisioning (except software as a service, on cloud)
Code definition: Provision of leased software applications from a centralized, hosted, and managed computing environment, customized to the needs of each clients, except software as a service (SaaS), cloud-based or on demand.

Code title: Software as a service, on cloud
Code definition: Provision of rented or leased software applications over the Internet, from a centralized, Internet-hosted, and managed cloud computing multi tenant environment, where all clients can use the same application, on demand, commonly (not exclusively) on a monthly or an annual fee basis. No installation of the application software is needed for the client.

This subclass comprises a service that analyzes the way a business process is conducted, and identifies improvements that can be made by integrating existing and new software services, in order to improve information flows and increase automation of the process.

Services that analyze the way a business process is conducted, and identifies improvements that can be made by integrating existing and new software services, in order to improve information flows and increase automation of the process.

Code title: Other information technology (IT) infrastructure provisioning services
Code definition: This subclass comprises other information technology (IT) hosting or infrastructure provisioning services such as hosting client's application, processing client's data and computer time share.

Code title: Information technology (IT) infrastructure co-location services (except telecommunications facilities)
Code definition: Information technology (IT) infrastructure co-location services, except telecommunications facilities, which provide storage capacity and Internet connections for rental to multiple retail clients.
Services of providing the infrastructure and the management or administration of the storage and back-up of data.
Services of providing the infrastructure and on-going management and administration of data as an organizational resource.

Code title: Video and audio streaming infrastructure provisioning services
Code definition: Services of providing the infrastructure for sending audio and video data over the Internet or providing services to support video and audio streaming over the Internet.

Code title: Infrastructure as a service (except data storage infrastructure provisioning)
Code definition: Infrastructure as a service (except data storage infrastructure provisioning).

Platform as a service (PaaS), or application platform as a service (aPaaS), refers to a category of cloud computing services that allows customers to provision, run, and manage a modular bundle of one or more applications and based on IT infrastructure as a service.

Code title: Other information technology (IT) infrastructure provisioning services, n.e.c.
Code definition: Other information technology (IT) infrastructure provisioning services, n.e.c.

Code title: Information technology (IT) infrastructure and network management services
Code definition: This subclass comprises the service of managing and monitoring a client's information technology (IT) infrastructure including hardware, software and networks.

Services of managing and monitoring communication networks and connected hardware to diagnose networking problems and gather capacity and usage statistics for the administration and fine-tuning of network traffic.
Providing day-to-day management and operation of a client's computer system.
This subclass comprises the provision of technical expertise and equipment to transform information and documents from one format or media to another.

Code title: Imaging and other data capture services
Code definition: Services of converting paper documents into digital or other machine-readable formats. These services generally involve the following components: document preparation; scanning, optical character recognition, and other data capture activities; and the delivery or output of the information captured into a database or a physical medium.
Services of moving data from one storage device to another or from one file format to another.
This class comprises other information services.
This subclass comprises other information services.
Providing access to library resources.
Providing access to archives, and other archive-related services.
Collecting, disseminating or providing access to information, n.e.c.

This group comprises financial system regulatory services; account and cash management products; loans and other credit financing products; investment products; financial planning services and trust products for individuals, businesses, institutions (except unincorporated) and governments; and products supporting financial services.

This class comprises services provided by central banks, other government agencies, and self-regulatory bodies (such as stock exchanges) to regulate financial systems and markets, and the participants in those systems and markets.

This subclass comprises services provided by central banks, other government agencies, and self-regulatory bodies (such as stock exchanges) to regulate securities markets and the participants in securities markets.
Services provided by central banks, other government agencies, and self-regulatory bodies (such as stock exchanges) to regulate securities markets and the participants in securities markets.
This subclass comprises services provided by central banks, other government agencies, and self-regulatory bodies to regulate credit markets and the participants in credit markets.
Services provided by central banks, other government agencies, and self-regulatory bodies to regulate credit markets and the participants in credit markets.
This subclass comprises services provided by central banks, other government agencies, and self-regulatory bodies to regulate insurance markets and the participants in insurance markets.
Services provided by central banks, other government agencies, and self-regulatory bodies to regulate insurance markets and the participants in insurance markets.

This class comprises money management services, provided to customers by means of deposit accounts, such as chequing, savings and time accounts, and specialized cash management services that enable businesses to handle cash, transfer monies, and in general make and receive payments.

This subclass comprises bundled services related to deposit accounts (cheques, account statements, automated banking machine (ABM) transactions, etc.) provided for a flat fee, usually paid monthly. Non-deposit services, such as traveller's cheques, may be included in deposit account service packages.

Bundled services related to deposit accounts (cheques, account statements, automated banking machine (ATM) transactions, etc.) provided for a flat fee, usually paid monthly. Non-deposit services, such as traveller's cheques, may be included in deposit account service packages.
This subclass comprises services related to deposit accounts, sold on an individual basis.
Services related to deposit accounts, sold on an individual basis.
This subclass comprises specialized deposit account and cash management services provided to businesses and government.
Specialized deposit account and cash management services provided to businesses and government.
This subclass comprises issuing documents that can be used as payment instruments.
Issuing documents that can be used as payment instruments.
This subclass comprises exchanging the currency of one country for that of another in small amounts, for a fee or commission.
Exchanging the currency of one country for that of another in small amounts, for a fee or commission.

This class comprises loans that represent the direct lending of funds under legal contract, either unsecured or secured by the assets being financed or by other assets, but without the exchange or the use of securities as collateral.

This subclass comprises loans to businesses. Loans represent the direct lending of funds under legal contract, either unsecured or secured by the assets being financed or by other assets, but without the exchange or the use of securities as collateral.

Loans to businesses. Loans represent the direct lending of funds under legal contract, either unsecured or secured by the assets being financed or by other assets, but without the exchange or the use of securities as collateral.
This subclass comprises loans to government.
Loans to government.
This subclass comprises loans to households.
Mortgage loans provided to owner-occupiers, secured by residential real property.
Loans and lines of credit secured by the equity of a borrower's residence.

Code title: Secured home loans (except residential mortgage and home equity loans) to households
Code definition: Secured or guaranteed home loans to households, except residential mortgage and home equity loans.
Loans to households for purchasing automobiles and other vehicles, secured by the vehicle.

Code title: Other secured consumer loans to households, n.e.c.
Code definition: Other secured loans to households, n.e.c.
Loans and lines of credit, not secured by collateral, for personal uses.
This class comprises credit card services; factoring; financial leasing; and sales financing.

This subclass comprises the provision of lines of credit to credit card holders, and credit card processing services to merchants, that together enable credit cards to be accepted as a means of payment.

Code title: Credit card cardholder products for businesses and government
Code definition: Provision of a revolving line of credit to business and government holders of credit cards, allowing them to purchase goods and services from merchants who accept their card. Credit granted through credit cards may be unsecured, or secured by a deposit held by the card issuer.

Code title: Credit card cardholder products to consumers
Code definition: Provision of a revolving line of credit to consumer holders of credit cards, allowing them to purchase goods and services from merchants who accept their card. Credit granted through credit cards may be unsecured, or secured by a deposit held by the card issuer.
Credit card transaction processing services provided by processors and banks to merchant account holders.
Services provided by credit card associations to issuing banks.

This subclass comprises the provision of financing to a business from the sale of its accounts receivable to a third party, known as a factor. Normally, the factor assumes the full risk of collection, including credit losses.
Financing provided to a business from the sale of its accounts receivable to a third party, known as a factor. Normally, the factor assumes the full risk of collection, including credit losses.

This subclass comprises leases in which the lessor is providing a financial service to enable the lessee to enjoy the benefits of ownership of the leased asset. A lessee has the option of purchasing the machinery and equipment after the lease term has been completed, at an agreed price. With a finance lease the equipment appears on the lessee's balance sheet, as it is viewed as a purchase. Also known as capital lease.

Motor vehicle leases in which the lessor is providing a financial service to enable the lessee to enjoy the benefits of ownership of the leased asset. A lessee has the option of purchasing the motor vehicle after the lease term has been completed, at an agreed price. With a finance lease the motor vehicle appears on the lessee's balance sheet, as it is viewed as a purchase.

Leases (except for motor vehicles) in which the lessor is providing a financial service to enable the lessee to enjoy the benefits of ownership of the leased asset. A lessee has the option of purchasing the machinery and equipment after the lease term has been completed, at an agreed price. With a finance lease the equipment appears on the lessee's balance sheet, as it is viewed as a purchase.
This subclass comprises the provision of credit by means of conditional sales contracts.
Providing credit by means of conditional sales contracts for purchases by businesses.
Providing credit by means of conditional sales contracts for purchases by consumers.

This class comprises financing services related to trading and dealing in securities which generally involve the use of securities as collateral or as the lent instrument, as well as other credit financing products, n.e.c.

This subclass comprises financing services related to trading and dealing in securities which generally involve the use of securities as collateral or as the lent instrument, as well as other credit financing products, n.e.c.
Collateralized lending of securities, to be returned on a specific date or on demand, paid for by fees based on the value of the loaned securities.
The sale of a security (often Treasury Bills) to a counterparty for cash with an agreement to repurchase it at a fixed price on a specified future date.
Provision of credit by means other than loans, credit cards, factoring, leasing, instalment credit products, and financing related to securities lending and repurchase agreements.
This class comprises securities origination products; brokering and dealing of financial instruments; and brokerage correspondent products.

This subclass comprises assisting the issuers of securities (businesses and government) in creating their securities and in having them distributed to the investing public. The service may involve advising the issuer; purchasing securities from the issuer and selling them (underwriting); or acting as an agent in marketing the securities.

Assisting the issuers of securities (businesses and government) in creating their securities and in having them distributed to the investing public. The service may involve advising the issuer; purchasing securities from the issuer and selling them (underwriting); or acting as an agent in marketing the securities.

Code title: Brokering and dealing of money market instruments
Code definition: This subclass comprises brokering and dealing money market instruments, which are fixed-rate of return debt instruments that mature within one year or less.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, negotiable certificates of deposit
Code definition: Brokering and dealing negotiable certificates of deposit, with a term of one year or less.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, commercial paper issued by financial institutions
Code definition: Brokering and dealing commercial paper issued by financial institutions, with a term of one year or less.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, commercial paper issued by non-financial institutions
Code definition: Brokering and dealing commercial paper issued by non-financial institutions, with a term of one year or less.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, bankers' acceptances
Code definition: Brokering and dealing bankers' acceptances, with a term of one year or less.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, Treasury bills
Code definition: Brokering and dealing Treasury bills, with a term of one year or less.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, other money market instruments
Code definition: Brokering and dealing money market instruments other than commercial paper, bankers' acceptances, negotiable certificates of deposit, or Treasury bills.

Code title: Brokering and dealing of other debt instruments
Code definition: This subclass comprises brokering and dealing debt instruments other than money market instruments.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, corporate bonds and asset-backed securities
Code definition: Brokering and dealing medium- and long-term corporate notes and bonds, and asset-backed securities.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, national government notes and bonds
Code definition: Brokering and dealing medium- and long-term bonds issued by the Government of Canada.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, provincial and local government notes and bonds
Code definition: Brokering and dealing medium- and long-term bonds issued by provincial and local governments.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, foreign government notes and bonds
Code definition: Brokering and dealing notes and bonds issued by foreign governments.
This subclass comprises brokering and dealing equity securities.
Brokering and dealing equity securities.
This subclass comprises brokering and dealing in derivative instruments, which are contracts whose value is based on the value of an underlying entity.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, futures contracts, exchange-traded
Code definition: Brokering and dealing futures contracts on exchanges.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, option contracts, exchange-traded
Code definition: Brokering and dealing option contracts on exchanges.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, forward contracts, traded over-the-counter
Code definition: Brokering and dealing forward contracts over-the-counter.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, swaps, traded over-the-counter
Code definition: Brokering and dealing swap contracts over-the-counter.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, option contracts, traded over-the-counter
Code definition: Brokering and dealing option contracts over-the-counter.

Code title: Brokering and dealing products, other derivatives contracts, traded over-the-counter
Code definition: Brokering and dealing derivative contracts, other than forward, swap or option contracts, over-the-counter.

Code title: Foreign currency wholesale brokering and dealing
Code definition: This subclass comprises brokering and dealing foreign currencies, on a wholesale basis.

Code title: Foreign currency wholesale brokering and dealing
Code definition: Brokering and dealing foreign currencies, on a wholesale basis.

Code title: Brokering and dealing of investment company securities
Code definition: This subclass comprises brokering and dealing investment company securities.

Code title: Brokering and dealing of investment company securities
Code definition: Brokering and dealing investment company securities.

Code title: Brokering and dealing of other financial instruments
Code definition: This subclass comprises brokering and dealing other financial instruments.

Code title: Brokerage or dealing services of cryptocurrency (virtual currency)
Code definition: Brokerage or dealing services of cryptocurrency (virtual currency).

Code title: Brokering and dealing of other financial instruments
Code definition: Brokering and dealing of other financial instruments.

Service consisting of one broker-dealer carrying out trades on behalf of another, where the first broker-dealer has access to a particular securities exchange and the other does not.

Code title: Personal trust and financial planning services
Code definition: This class comprises trust services and financial planning and investment management services intended for private individuals.

Code title: Personal trust and financial planning services
Code definition: This subclass comprises trust services and financial planning and investment management services intended for private individuals.

Services to establish and administer trusts, under which a trustee holds legal title to property belonging to another, for the benefit of a beneficiary. Trusts are defined by an agreement, contract, declaration in a will, or order of a court.

Code title: Personal financial planning and investment management services
Code definition: Financial planning and investment management services for individuals.

Code title: Trust and financial planning services for businesses, institutions, and government
Code definition: This class comprises trust services and financial planning and investment management services for businesses, institutions (except unincorporated), and governments.

Code title: Trust and financial planning services for businesses, institutions, and government
Code definition: This subclass comprises trust services and financial planning and investment management services for businesses, institutions (except unincorporated), and governments.

Code title: Trust services for businesses, institutions (except unincorporated), and governments
Code definition: Services to establish and administer trusts for businesses, institutions (except unincorporated), and governments.

Code title: Financial planning and investment management services for businesses, institutions (except unincorporated), and governments
Code definition: Financial planning and investment management services for businesses, institutions (except unincorporated), and governments.

Code title: Tax planning and consulting services for businesses (except unincorporated) and governments
Code definition: Tax planning and consulting services for businesses (except unincorporated) and governments.
This class comprises management of financial market and clearing products; automated clearing house products; and other products supporting financial services.

Code title: Management of financial market and clearing services
Code definition: This subclass comprises the provision of an infrastructure for trading securities and commodity contracts; and clearing and settlement services for securities, commodities contracts, and payments. Covers trades executed on exchanges or over-the-counter, and clearing and settlement services for those trades.
Clearing and settling payments for financial transactions other than trades of securities and commodity contracts.

Code title: Security and commodity contract trade execution, clearing and settlement services
Code definition: Executing, clearing and settling trades of securities and commodity contracts and other financial instruments.

Code title: Services of access to security and commodity contract trade execution and clearing systems
Code definition: Providing broker-dealers with access to securities or commodity contract trading systems, whether live floor exchanges or electronic systems.

Code title: Security and commodity contract exchange and clearing house listing services
Code definition: Listing securities and other financial instruments on trading, clearing and settlement systems.

Code title: Other management of financial market and clearing services
Code definition: Providing support services for trading, clearing and settling securities and commodities contracts and financial payments, n.e.c.
This subclass comprises automated funds credit and debit clearing and settlement services.
Automated funds credit and debit clearing and settlement services.
This subclass comprises loan servicing; automated banking machine (ABM) operation products; and other miscellaneous products supporting financial services.

Loan servicing entails the processing of payments of principal and interest, the maintenance of associated accounts such as escrow accounts for the payment of taxes and insurance, and the provision of loan information.
Use of automated banking machines (ABMs) not associated with the user's financial institution.

Code title: Other miscellaneous products supporting financial services
Code definition: Products supporting financial services, n.e.c.
This group comprises pension and annuity products; and life insurance products.

This class comprises underwriting services of plans which provide income payments at regular intervals to individuals or members of groups. Plans may require a single contribution or a series of contributions; may be compulsory or optional; may have nominal benefits determined in advance or dependent on the market value of aspects supporting the plan; and, if related to employment, may or may not be portable with a change in employment. The duration of the period during which benefits are paid may be fixed in terms of a minimum or maximum; there may or may not be survivors' benefits.

This subclass comprises underwriting services of plans which provide income payments at regular intervals to individuals or members of groups.
